name: Tello Charging Dock
summary: A landing pad for a DJI Tello drone. Copper pads on the drone's four feet meet copper-lined cups in a wood block. A diode bridge on the drone makes polarity irrelevant, so the drone charges whichever way it lands. An MT3608 boost board set to 5.8 V feeds the cups through a 1 A polyfuse.

parts.name: Copper foil tape
parts.detail: LOVIMAG, conductive adhesive. Used on the feet and in the cups.
parts.identify: A roll of shiny copper-colored foil with a paper backing. Thin, bends and tears easily, roughly 5 to 10 mm wide.

parts.name: B5819W Schottky diode
parts.detail: Chanzon, pack of 100. The four of them form the bridge.
parts.identify: Very small black surface-mount part (SOD-123 package), about 3.5 mm long, two flat metal ends, a single silver or white stripe near one end. The stripe marks the cathode. Easy to confuse with other SMD diodes in the pack; the pack label says B5819W or SS14.

parts.name: Right-angle micro-USB cable
parts.detail: BAIRONG. Supplies the plug that goes into the drone's side port and the four wires.
parts.identify: USB cable whose small end is a micro-USB plug bent 90 degrees. Inside the sheath: red (+), black (−), white and green (data, spares).

parts.name: MT3608 boost board, USB-C
parts.detail: AKEYSRC, pack of 6. Powers the dock.
parts.identify: Small rectangular PCB (about 36 × 17 mm) with a USB-C socket on one end, a square black inductor, a tiny chip, and a small blue or white multi-turn trim pot with a brass screw. Pads labelled OUT+ and OUT−.

parts.name: 1 A polyfuse RF16-100
parts.detail: Pack of 10. Cuts power on a short.
parts.identify: Yellow or orange flat disc with two thin wire legs, like a tiny yellow lentil. Resettable fuse, no polarity.

parts.name: Countersink drill bit
parts.detail: Or any 12 to 20 mm bit, drilled shallow.
parts.identify: Cone-shaped bit, usually with a point and fluted sides.

parts.name: Heat-shrink tubing
parts.identify: Short lengths of thin black plastic tube that shrink with heat.

parts.name: Soldering iron, solder, multimeter, scissors
parts.detail: The multimeter is not optional: it sets the 5.8 V.

parts.name: Scrap wood and a phone charger
parts.detail: Wood about 15 × 15 cm. Any USB charger and cable.

notNeeded: The MTDELE USB-C breakout. The MT3608 board already has USB-C.

steps.title: What you need
steps.caption: Five parts from your cart, a scrap of wood and a few tools. Any phone charger powers the dock.
checks: All five bought parts present: copper tape, 4 diodes, micro-USB cable, MT3608 board, polyfuse.
Wood block about 15 × 15 cm, thick enough to drill 5 mm cups.
Tools: soldering iron, multimeter, drill with countersink or 12 to 20 mm bit, scissors, heat-shrink.

steps.title: Cut the cable
steps.caption: Cut about 10 cm from the plug and keep the plug end. Strip the four wires: red is +, black is −, the other two are spares. Confirm red is + with the multimeter.
checks: The piece kept is the micro-USB plug end with about 10 cm of cable.
Four wires exposed: red, black, white, green. Red and black stripped; white and green can be trimmed or taped off.
Multimeter in continuity or diode mode confirms red goes to the + pin of the micro-USB plug (pin 1, at the wide edge) and black to −.

steps.title: Make the diode bridge
steps.caption: Solder four diodes into a diamond, with each stripe facing exactly as drawn. Red wire on top, black on the bottom, one feet wire on each side. Cover it with heat-shrink.
checks: Four diodes form a diamond. Both stripes (cathodes) point toward the TOP node, which is the red (+) wire. Both unstriped ends (anodes) meet at the BOTTOM node, which is the black (−) wire.
Left node joins one diode's anode and another diode's cathode; same for the right node. Left node is feet pair A, right node is feet pair B.

Meter check in diode mode: from either side node to the top node reads about 0.2 to 0.4 V one way (Schottky drop), open the other way. Side to bottom node reads the same drop in the opposite direction.
Bridge wrapped in heat-shrink or tape so no diode leg can touch another.

steps.title: Copper on every foot
steps.caption: Wrap a small piece of copper tape over the tip of a foot with its wire tucked underneath, then add a dab of solder. Do all four feet.
checks: A stripped wire end sits UNDER the copper tape, on the foot tip, and a small solder blob bonds wire to tape.
Tape wraps the bottom of the foot, the surface that touches the ground.
All four feet done. Wires are thin enough not to lift the foot.

steps.title: Wire the feet in pairs
steps.caption: Each diagonal pair of feet shares one side of the bridge. Tape the wires flat under the arms and keep the belly vents and sensors uncovered.
checks: Front-left and rear-right feet both go to the bridge's LEFT node (pair A). Front-right and rear-left both go to the RIGHT node (pair B). Diagonals, never two feet on the same side.
Wires run along the underside of the arms, taped flat.
Nothing covers the belly: the downward vision sensors, the IR sensors and the vent slots stay clear.

steps.title: Plug it in
steps.caption: Push the plug into the side port and leave it there. Tape the bridge and wires flat. The drone side is done.
checks: Micro-USB plug fully seated in the Tello's side port and left in place.
Bridge taped flat against the body, not dangling near the props.
Drone still balances level on its four feet.

steps.title: Mark the feet
steps.caption: Stand the drone on paper and mark where the four feet touch. Copy the marks onto the wood.
checks: Four marks on the paper matching the drone's footprint (roughly a square).
Same four marks transferred to the top of the wood block, centered.

steps.title: Drill four cups
steps.caption: At each mark, drill a shallow cone about 5 mm deep and 2 to 3 times wider than a foot. Drill a small hole through the middle for a wire.
checks: Each cup is a shallow cone, about 5 mm deep, wide enough that a foot landing a few mm off still slides to the center.
A small through-hole (2 to 3 mm) at the bottom of each cup for the wire.
Four cups total, no splintering that would stop the foot from seating.

steps.title: Line the cups with copper
steps.caption: Cut a square of tape, slit the edges and press it into the cup. Do all four. Keep the cups separate: no tape running between them.
checks: Each cup's inner cone is covered in copper tape, pressed smooth, the through-hole left open.
No copper tape bridging between any two cups on the top surface. Each cup is electrically separate from the others.

steps.title: Set the board to 5.8 V
steps.caption: Plug the charger into the board with nothing else connected. Hold the meter on OUT+ and OUT− and turn the small screw until it reads 5.8 V.
checks: USB-C charger plugged into the MT3608 board, nothing on OUT+ / OUT−.
Multimeter on DC volts, red probe on OUT+, black on OUT−.
Trim-pot screw turned until the display reads 5.80 V (within about 0.05 V). Clockwise usually raises the voltage, but many turns may be needed on a multi-turn pot.
Never connect the drone before the board reads 5.8 V.

steps.title: Wire under the block
steps.caption: Push a wire up each hole and solder it to the copper. Under the block, join the diagonal cups: one pair to OUT+ through the fuse, the other pair to OUT−.
checks: A wire comes up through each of the four holes and is soldered to the copper inside the cup.
Underneath, two DIAGONAL cups are joined and go to OUT+ via the polyfuse in series. The other two diagonal cups are joined and go to OUT−.
The fuse is in the + leg between the board's OUT+ and the cups.
No wire on the underside shorts + to −.

steps.title: Test by hand
steps.caption: Two neighboring cups should read 5.8 V. Set the drone in the cups and watch for its charging light. No light? Turn the drone off and try again.
checks: Meter across any two NEIGHBORING cups reads about 5.8 V. Across two diagonal cups it reads 0 V.
Drone placed in the cups, powered off: its charging LED comes on within a few seconds.
If no light: check each foot's copper touches its cup, and re-check the diode bridge orientation.

steps.title: Land and charge
steps.caption: When the drone lands, copper touches copper and the battery charges, the same as plugging in a cable.
checks: Landing on the dock from flight seats all four feet in the cups.
Charging LED on after landing.

safety: The soldering iron tip is 300 °C or more. Rest it in its stand.
Set the board to 5.8 V before anything is connected to its output. Over-voltage can damage the Tello.
The polyfuse protects against a short between + and − cups, not against reversed voltage. The diode bridge handles polarity.
Keep copper tape, wires and solder blobs away from the propellers and the belly sensors.
